newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-REDSKINS RE-SIGN FREE AGENT RB TERRY ALLEN.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-REDSKINS RE-SIGN FREE AGENT RB TERRY ALLEN.

text.p: The Washington Redskins held on to their star running back Terry Allen, re-signing the unrestricted free agent to a four-year contract, the team announced Wednesday.
Allen led the National Football League with 21 touchdowns and finished with a single-season Redskins-record 1,353 yards -- third best in the NFC and sixth in the league.
"There is no question in anyone's mind that Terry Allen is one of the premier running backs in this league," said Redskins general manager Charley Casserly.
The 5-10 (1.78 m), 208-pound (94 kg) Allen, who turned 29 last week, had rushing touchdowns in 11 games last season and led all non-kickers with 126 points in earning his first trip to the Pro Bowl.

Allen has played seven seasons in the NFL, the last two with Washington. He was drafted in the ninth round in 1990 by the Minnesota Vikings and signed with the Redskins before the 1995 season as an unrestricted free agent.

Allen joined Barry Sanders of the Detroit Lions, Dallas Cowboy Emmitt Smith and Thurman Thomas of the Buffalo Bills as the only running backs in the league to top 1,000 yards in each of the last three seasons.
He has compiled 5,457 yards and 54 rushing touchdowns in his career.
